channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Carnell Tate (shoulder) worked out with trainers on the side during Thursday’s practice.
item.description: He may not elevate beyond an official DNP today, but this is an actual step after Tate missed four consecutive practices and Week 8 sandwiched around their Week 9 bye. He’ll have a non-zero chance to play this week heading into Friday, but you have to imagine the best we’ll see on Friday is a questionable tag.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Woody Marks (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Per Aaron Wilson, he injured the knee in Wednesday’s practice and was experiencing discomfort. We don’t necessarily think Marks is in major trouble yet considering “discomfort” isn’t exactly a major injury, and he has been remarkably durable in game. But there is certainly a chance he’ll miss Week 10’s game against the Browns and fantasy managers should be prepared to pivot on Friday.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said to “expect a lot of Cam Skattebo” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
item.description: The Giants host the Commanders for this week’s Thursday Night Football game. The open-air stadium is currently experiencing heavy rain, and Fowler indicates the rainfall will continue this evening. Devin Singletary will back up Skattebo, but the touch distribution will heavily “slant” toward Skattebo, solidifying his status as an RB2.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: David Montgomery (groin) returned to practice on Thursday.
item.description: Montgomery was mostly working out with a trainer, but DeMeco Ryans said they were “pleased with the progress he was making.” It’s possible this goes down as a DNP still on the official report, but it is real progress that he’s back on the field and he now has a non-zero chance to suit up for Week 10.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Packers coach Matt LaFleur indicated that Luke Musgrave (neck) “probably” will not play in 2026.
item.description: Earlier this season, the Packers thought that Musgrave had a chance to return. Unfortunately, it appears as though that is no longer the case. The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Musgrave’s “tenure with the Packers is all but over.”-Nic Bodiford

item.title: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes the Packers should not sign MarShawn Lloyd to an extension after next season.
item.description: Schneidman believes it is “not possible” to sign Lloyd to an extension after the 2027 season because of the young running back’s poor play. Lloyd is still trying to beat defenders around the edge with speed, rather than running north-south when he needs to. Although the injuries are mostly behind him, he has failed to live up to preseason expectations. Lloyd does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports the 49ers and Chiefs “were interested” in Garrett Wilson ahead of the trade deadline.
item.description: The Jets made it clear they were not moving Wilson early in the process, so we can’t imagine trade talks between them and either team made it very far. Cimini notes that the Jets could revisit a Wilson trade in the offseason. Wilson told reporters earlier this year that he loves it in New York, but he loves winning more. The Jets haven’t done much of that since Wilson was drafted. This will be a storyline to watch in the offseason, though we suspect he’ll remain in New York for the forseeable future.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Former Bucs head coach Bruce Arians says he has “the itch” to coach football again.
item.description: Arians detailed myriad health issues that he dealt with in his final season as the Bucs’ head coach. He tore his Achilles and eventually injured his back. Arians was also monitoring an aneurysm in his heart at the time. He stepped away from coaching after the 2021 season but remained with the Bucs in an advisory role for some time. Arians won 13 games in his final season as a head coach and took home the Lombardi Trophy in his penultimate season. Now 74 years old, Arians wouldn’t be the long-term answer for a team, but he could be an option for a team in a win-now window. He later stated that he would consider returning to the Bucs and is only interested in a head-coaching role.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Bengals designated Andrei Iosivas (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
item.description: Iosivas will practice today for the first time since injuring his thumb in Week 2. The Bengals have 21 days to officially activate him from injured reserve. He will likely reclaim his No. 3 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Ravens signed K Harrison Mevis to their practice squad.
item.description: The team added Riley Patterson to their active roster yesterday, but both kickers will likely have a chance to earn the job in practice this week. We aren’t expecting great fantasy numbers from either kicker with Lamar Jackson no longer fueling the offense.-Kyle Dvorchak
